findings.title: End-card ticks now advance, but the telemetry accumulator and the checkpoint rule do not say whether it keeps counting, and restoring a capture from the end card would corrupt the round summary
findings.claim: The R1-F2 fix keeps ticks advancing on a decided round. Today recordTick relies on a decided duel not advancing: it ignores a call only when the tick did not advance. On every end-card tick it would therefore keep adding to t.ticks and the per-tick counters (helm and weapons empty ticks, enemyInArcTicks, weaponsIdleTicks, walkingTicks and repairingTicks). Its terminal-cause block also rewrites t.terminal on every tick while a hull is 0. Each end-card tick shows no new contacts or events, so the causes are reset to []. The new validator rule makes this worse: telemetry ticks must equal tick − baseTick, which forces the accumulator to keep counting on the end card. The live summary is computed once, at the decision. But rules.restore rebuilds it from the restored telemetry through session(). So a capture on the end card (pause, periodic, a Net-3e mirror, or the safe point at duel:<round>:true once later ticks pass) restores with a longer round, inflated counters and empty terminal causes. That summary is the one §8 says the host's checkpoint memory provides for a missed round.
findings.evidence: spec L243 (ticks keep advancing), L235 and L264 (telemetry ticks = tick − baseTick), L255 (the accumulator restarts per round), L282 ('the memory schema is unchanged … its ticks counts from baseTick'), §8 (the host's checkpoint memory holds the round), L389 (telemetry continues across a restore); telemetry.ts:L87-92 (recordTick skips only when the tick did not advance, a call after the end is 'ignored'), L145-150 (per-tick counters), L153-161 (terminal causes recomputed whenever the outcome is not Running); duelRules.ts:L21 (session() recomputes the summary from telemetry on restore), L36-37 (recordTick every step, summary set once), L61; duelCheckpoint.ts:L99
findings.why: The end-card restore tests in §10 would either fail or pin a wrong summary. The §16 report's round length, the empty and idle ratios, and the terminal causes would be wrong for any round recovered from a checkpoint. A planner has to decide the accumulator's semantics on the end card.
findings.fix: State that the accumulator freezes once a round is decided: recordTick ignores decided ticks other than the deciding one. Change the checkpoint rule to: telemetry ticks = tick − baseTick while the outcome is Running, and = decidedTick − baseTick once it is decided. Keep decidedTick in the round module, or derive it from the frozen ticks. Add a test that captures on the end card N ≥ 60 ticks after the decision, restores, and checks that the restored summary (ticks, terminal causes, counters) equals the round record emitted at the decision.

The trigger and the origin are now specified. The ordering is not well defined. L196 says the pause takes effect 'after the presence command is admitted'. Admitted is not executed. A lifecycle pause is applied in applyControls (core.ts:L376-428), separately from executeTick (L430-433). If the pause lands before the next tick, presence stays in `pending` for the whole pause. Then capture is skipped (core.ts:L127 refuses while anything is pending), so there is no pause checkpoint or mirror during the outage. Presence's result also arrives only after resume, so the 'presence false, then the pause' test (L198) has no defined observable. Fix: the manager calls pause('peer-lost') only once the steward's presence command has an applied result, at least one tick later. The test then asserts that presence's applied tick is before the pause boundary and that a pause capture is delivered.
The round, the seed and helmPlayer come from hashed state; host records are authoritative; the transport comes from the guest; reconnect tests cover mid-round and across a round end.
